Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

final adjective

not to be changed: a final decision

also that’s final, final decision, final answer, definitive, settled, period (that’s final), and that’s that, I have spoken

classical

Liv. 2.45.13: certum atque dēcrētum est nōn dare signum
Plaut. Bacch. 382: certumst jam dīcam patrī
Cic. Rosc. Am. 31: certum est dēlīberātumque (Lewis & Short)

certum (atque dēcrētum) est

phrase; with an infinitive, “I have made up my mind to”

it is settled, that’s final

The speaker’s last word on a matter: my mind is made up (see decide, and sure).

Other words

  • ratus, rata, ratum — settled, fixed, valid, not to be undone

    adjective (participle of reor): ratum esse, ratum habēre · classical · Cic. Ac. 2.27: dēcrētum stabile, fīxum, ratum esse dēbeat (Lewis & Short); Ter. Ph. 951: quod modo erat ratum, irritum est

    Ratum habēre, to treat as final, to confirm; its opposite is irritus, void.

  • fīxus, fīxa, fīxum — fixed, settled

    adjective (participle of fīgō) · also used · classical · Cic. Clu. 132: fīxās et in perpetuum ratās (Lewis & Short)

  • Dīxī. — I have spoken: that’s final, period

    perfect of dīcō, closing what one has said · also used · classical · Traupman 105: I’ll not give in, period, nōn concēdam, dīxī

    “I have said (it)”: Traupman uses it to close an argument. The pronouncement that cannot be changed is certum est (above).

  • fīnālis, fīnāle — of boundaries; (late) final

    adjective, third declension · avoid · late Latin · Dig. 10.1.11 (Lewis & Short); Macr. Somn. 2.5; Aug. Civ. 19.4 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 45, 375 (final whistle, final score)

    Post-classical: a surveyors’ and lawyers’ word for boundaries, and “final” only in late philosophy (causa fīnālis). Traupman uses it for the final whistle and the final score.

Examples

  • itaque certum atque dēcrētum est nōn dare signum, nisi victōrēs sē reditūrōs ex hāc pugnā jūrant

    so my decision is final: I will not give the signal unless they swear they will come back from this battle victoriousLiv. 2.45.13

  • Quod dictum, indictum est: quod modo erat ratum, irritum est.

    What was said is unsaid; what was settled a moment ago is void.Ter. Ph. 950–951

  • Nōn concēdam, dīxī.

    I won’t give in, period.Traupman 105

See also last, sure, decide.
